questions.q: How does PCA applied to a panel of asset returns relate to classical statistical factor models like the APT?
options: PCA requires the factors to be specified in advance, exactly like APT
PCA finds variance-maximizing directions with no assumption about what the factors are, which empirically often resemble real common factors
PCA and factor models are unrelated techniques used for completely different purposes
PCA only works on labeled factor data
questions.explain: PCA makes no assumptions about what the underlying factors are — it purely finds the directions of maximum variance. Applied to broad return panels, those directions often resemble real factors like a market factor, approximating a statistical factor model.

questions.q: Why are returns standardized (e.g. with StandardScaler) before fitting PCA?
options: Standardization is only cosmetic and does not affect PCA's output
Without it, high-volatility assets would dominate the variance the components chase, independent of real common structure
PCA cannot run on non-integer data
Standardization removes the need for explained_variance_ratio_
questions.explain: PCA is sensitive to scale. Without standardizing, a few high-volatility names would dominate the variance components purely due to scale, not genuine shared structure.

questions.q: Why is the first principal component of a broad equity returns panel often informally called the "market factor"?
options: Because sklearn labels it that way automatically
Because it is computed from index futures prices only
Because it typically loads positively on nearly every asset, reflecting broad co-movement with the overall market
Because it always explains exactly 100% of the variance
questions.explain: PC1 in a broad equity panel almost always loads positively across nearly all assets, since most stocks move with the market to some degree — hence the informal name, even though PCA was never told what 'the market' is.

options: The correlation between each asset and the market
The fraction of total variance in the data attributed to each principal component
The number of clusters recommended for the dataset
The p-value of each factor's statistical significance
questions.explain: explained_variance_ratio_ reports what fraction of total variance each component accounts for, letting you see how concentrated the variance is (e.g., PC1 alone explaining 30-50%+).

questions.q: How does ICA (Independent Component Analysis) differ from PCA as a factor-discovery tool?
options: ICA requires labeled data, PCA does not
ICA finds statistically independent components, while PCA only finds uncorrelated, variance-maximizing ones
ICA and PCA produce mathematically identical results in all cases
ICA can only be applied to clustering problems, not returns data
questions.explain: PCA finds orthogonal (uncorrelated) directions that maximize variance. ICA instead looks for components that are statistically independent, which can better separate distinct, non-Gaussian sources of variation.
